subject: SLA-backed pool sizing & concessions request
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@orchid.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@orchid.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing + committed discount ask

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost numbers looked promising. We are now pulling together an ask for our finance and procurement teams and need a concrete recommendation for a Dedicated (reserved) GPU pool that meets our production needs. High-level workload details below: 

- Models: mix of 13B/70B open weights (mainly 13B trimmed quantized variants + small number of 70B for batch tasks)
- Typical steady QPS: ~320 req/s (text generate, avg response ~120 tokens)
- Peak bursts: up to ~1,300 req/s for up to 20 minutes (marketing spikes)
- Typical concurrency distribution: baseline 200–400 concurrent, short peaks to 1,000–1,200 concurrent
- Average context length: 2,048 tokens; max 4,096 tokens on long-tail requests
- SLA ask: p95 latency < 300ms for the 13B path; 99.9% uptime; commercial credits for SLO misses

We are evaluating a 12-month reserved commit and would like to understand: 
1) Recommended GPU pool configuration (instance types / card count) to hit the steady + burst profile while keeping unit cost reasonable
2) Throughput guarantees you can commit to (and how burst credits would work)
3) Discount tiers for a 12-month commit (looking for ~20–30% off sticker)
4) Any recommended burst/overage mechanics and how you price those tokens/hours

I can share telemetry if it helps — I have a small sample of our request distribution attached. Can we get a preliminary sizing and a term sheet to circulate with procurement?

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform
Orchid.ai

[Attachment: orchid-workload-profile.csv (csv)]

From: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@orchid.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing + committed discount ask

Samir —

Appreciate the clear workload summary, that helps a lot. We took a quick pass with Ben and Karthik and put together an initial recommendation below. This is intentionally conservative on burst headroom; we can tighten if you can commit to telemetry sharing and a monthly usage baseline.

High-level recommendation (initial):
- Recommended pool: 8x H100-equivalent GPUs (multi-node pool), configured as 2x 4-GPU inference nodes.
  - Rationale: the 13B trimmed/quantized path maps efficiently to H100 runtime kernels; 8 cards give capacity for steady 300–400 req/s with room for parallelism and KV cache hit rate improvements.
- Estimated steady throughput: ~350–450 req/s (avg resp 120 tokens, 2k context)
- Peak headroom with burst credits: up to ~1,200–1,400 req/s for short windows (20 min) with automatic spill to additional pay-as-you-go capacity if sustained beyond burst budget
- Suggested commit: 12-month reserved commit covering ~75% of expected monthly GPU-hours (this reduces committed spend while leaving room for burst pay-go)

We put the modeling details into an attachment (pool-sizing-math.pdf) and a CSV for your telemetry; Ben will follow up with per-model token/sec assumptions.

Next steps: 
1) Ben to share a throughput model and assumptions by EOD tomorrow.
2) If this looks reasonable, we’ll produce a term sheet with tiered discount bands based on committed GPU-hours/month.
3) We’ll propose burst credit mechanics (short bursts included, overage billed at reduced pay-go rate).

Would you be available for a 30-min call on Monday to align with procurement?

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0124

[Attachment: pool-sizing-math.pdf (pdf)]

From: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@orchid.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing + committed discount ask

Samir / Lauren —

Following up with the throughput model and key assumptions so procurement has something concrete to review. Please see the short notes below and the attached CSV for per-minute distribution.

Assumptions used for the model:
- Model mix: 90% 13B-quantized path (costed as 0.45 GPU-seconds per 120-token response), 10% 70B batch jobs (costed as 6.0 GPU-seconds averaged across batching windows)
- Baseline steady-state: 320 req/s -> ~144 GPU-seconds/sec equivalent -> ~518,400 GPU-seconds / day (~144 GPU-hours/day)
- Peak 20-minute burst (1,300 req/s sustained for 20m): additional ~93k GPU-seconds across burst window (~25.9 GPU-hours)
- Monthly baseline (30-day) estimate: ~4,320 GPU-hours / month; with 25% headroom for variability target commit coverage = 3,240 GPU-hours/month

Sizing mapping:
- 8x H100-equivalent cards (24/7) = ~5,760 GPU-hours/month capacity (8 cards x 24h x 30d)
- If you reserve 3,240 GPU-hours/month (our suggested commit), that covers ~56% of 8-card pool usage; remaining capacity provides burst headroom and redundancy.

Pricing & discount bands (high level):
- Sticker pay-go list: $X per GPU-hour (we will redline real numbers in term sheet)
- 12-month commit @ 40% of sticker (commit covers 3,240 GPU-hours/mo) -> this is an example band; actual banding will be 20% / 25% / 30% at higher commits
- Included burst credits: 200 GPU-hours/month (absorbed at committed rate), thereafter overage billed at pay-go with a 15% markup vs committed unit

Risks & notes:
- If Orchid’s 70B batch load grows >15% of traffic, we’ll need an addon for batching capacity (costly if sustained)
- KV cache hit rate improvements can materially reduce GPU-hours — we can model a 10–20% saving if you can enable prefix caching for common prompts

I’ll translate the above into a term sheet draft (with real $ values) once we lock a commit target.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

[Attachment: orchid-workload-profile.csv (csv)]

From: Harper Lee <harper.legal@orchid.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@orchid.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:39:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing + committed discount ask

Hi Lauren / Karthik,

Procurement ran the numbers and has two asks before we proceed to SOW: 
1) Discount target: Orchid is pushing for a 25% concession off the term-sheet pricing for a 12-month commit that covers at least 60% of baseline monthly hours.
2) SLA credits: we need clearer SLO definitions (p95 latency broken out by model class) and a credit schedule (e.g., 5% credit for single-month miss >1% of requests).

They also asked whether Redwood can: 
- Provide a burst credit top-up mechanism for a one-time additional purchase if we anticipate a large campaign (e.g., marketed feature launch)
- Confirm that the Dedicated control plane can emit audit logs and token-level usage for our security team (SOC2 evidence will be needed)

Can you provide a brief redlined term-sheet and a yes/no on the audit logs? We want to keep this moving but need these pieces for legal/finance.

Best,
Harper Lee
Legal Counsel — Orchid.ai

--
Harper requested cc to procurement@orchid.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: Harper Lee <harper.legal@orchid.ai>, procurement@orchid.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing + committed discount ask

Harper / Team —

Thanks — and great questions. Short answers up front, then a proposed concession package so procurement can see trade-offs.

Audit logs / SOC2 evidence: yes — Redwood Dedicated control plane can emit token-level usage logs (redactable) and audit trails. We will include the SOC2 attestation in the enterprise package. Monica, I’m looping you to confirm retention windows and any additional compliance packaging.

SLA & credits (proposed):
- SLOs: p95 latency < 300ms for 13B path; p95 < 700ms for 70B batch during normal operation
- Credit schedule: single-month window miss >1% of eligible requests -> 5% monthly service credit; >5% -> 15% credit. Credits capped per contract.

Concession package (12-month commit scenario):
- Commit level: 3,500 GPU-hours/month (covers ~81% of the modeled baseline)
- Discount: 22% off sticker on committed hours; additional 4% discount (total 26%) if Orchid increases commit to 4,200 GPU-hours/month
- Burst mechanics: includes 300 GPU-hours/month of burst credits; one-time campaign top-up available at pre-agreed discounted pay-go rate (term sheet will list the unit price)
- SLA addendum: we’ll include the credit schedule and a 30-day remediation window before credit issuance to allow for mitigation

Next steps:
1) We’ll prepare a redlined term sheet with the above bands and real $ pricing to circulate (see attached draft).
2) Monica will confirm audit log retention options (7/30/90 day tiers).
3) If Orchid approves the commit band, we’ll prepare SOW + DocuSign route.

If that package looks acceptable we can aim to get a signed SOW by mid-June.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP Sales — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
